questions.question_text: Find the principal value of $\sin^{-1}(\frac{1}{2}) + \cos^{-1}(\frac{1}{2})$. [15-20 words]
questions.answer: Using the inverse trigonometric identity $\sin^{-1}(x) + \cos^{-1}(x) = \frac{\pi}{2}$ for $x \in [-1, 1]$. Therefore, substituting $x = \frac{1}{2}$ directly yields $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.question_text: If $2X + Y = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $Y = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$, find the matrix $X$. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: We have $2X = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$. Subtracting matrices gives $2X = \begin{pmatrix} -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -3 \end{pmatrix}$. Dividing by 2, we get $X = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ -1/2 & -3/2 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.question_text: Differentiate $y = x^x$ with respect to $x$ using logarithmic differentiation. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Taking natural logarithm, $\log y = x \log x$. Differentiating both sides yields $\frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx} = 1 \cdot \log x + x \cdot \frac{1}{x} = 1 + \log x$. Thus, $\frac{dy}{dx} = x^x(1 + \log x)$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the definite integral $\int_0^1 \frac{1}{1+x^2} \, dx$. [15-25 words]
questions.answer: The standard integral formula gives $\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} \, dx = \tan^{-1}x$. Applying the limits from $0$ to $1$, we compute $\tan^{-1}(1) - \tan^{-1}(0) = \frac{\pi}{4} - 0 = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.question_text: Find the interval in which the function $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 6$ is strictly increasing. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: First derivative is $f'(x) = 2x - 4$. For the function to be strictly increasing, $f'(x) > 0$. Thus, $2x - 4 > 0 \implies x > 2$. The interval is $(2, \infty)$.

questions.question_text: Express the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$ as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix. [30-45 words]
questions.answer: Let $P = \frac{1}{2}(A + A^T)$ and $Q = \frac{1}{2}(A - A^T)$. $A^T = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. $P = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 6 & 6 \\ 6 & -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 \\ 3 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. $Q = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Therefore, $A = P + Q$.

questions.question_text: Differentiate $\sin^2 x$ with respect to $e^{\cos x}$. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Let $u = \sin^2 x$ and $v = e^{\cos x}$. Compute $\frac{du}{dx} = 2\sin x \cos x$ and $\frac{dv}{dx} = -e^{\cos x} \sin x$. The derivative is $\frac{du}{dv} = \frac{2\sin x \cos x}{-e^{\cos x} \sin x} = -2\cos x \cdot e^{-\cos x}$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the indefinite integral $\int \frac{x}{(x-1)(x-2)} \, dx$ using partial fractions. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Let $\frac{x}{(x-1)(x-2)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{x-2}$. Multiplying gives $x = A(x-2) + B(x-1)$. Set $x=1$ to get $A = -1$. Set $x=2$ to get $B = 2$. The integral becomes $\int (\frac{-1}{x-1} + \frac{2}{x-2}) \, dx = -\log|x-1| + 2\log|x-2| + C$.

questions.question_text: Determine the value of the constant $k$ so that the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{\sin 3x}{5x}, & x \neq 0 \\ k, & x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=0$. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: For continuity at $x=0$, $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = f(0)$. We evaluate $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin 3x}{5x} = \frac{3}{5} \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin 3x}{3x} = \frac{3}{5}(1) = \frac{3}{5}$. Equating this to $f(0)=k$, we find $k = \frac{3}{5}$.

questions.question_text: Find the local maxima and local minima values of the function $f(x) = 3x^4 - 4x^3 - 12x^2 + 12$. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Calculate $f'(x) = 12x^3 - 12x^2 - 24x = 12x(x-2)(x+1)$. Critical points are $x=0, 2, -1$. $f''(x) = 36x^2 - 24x - 24$. At $x=0$, $f''(0) < 0$ (Local Max, value $12$). At $x=2$, $f''(2) > 0$ (Local Min, value $-20$). At $x=-1$, $f''(-1) > 0$ (Local Min, value $7$).

questions.question_text: Evaluate the definite integral $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^7 x \, dx$ by determining structural properties. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Let $f(x) = \sin^7 x$. We test for even/odd functionality. $f(-x) = \sin^7(-x) = -\sin^7 x = -f(x)$. Since the integrand is an odd function over a symmetric interval $[-a, a]$, the definite integral is exactly $0$.

questions.question_text: Solve the following system of linear equations using the matrix method: $3x - 2y + 3z = 8$, $2x + y - z = 1$, $4x - 3y + 2z = 4$. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Represent as $AX=B$, where $A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$, $X = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix}$, $B = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$. $|A| = 3(2-3) - (-2)(4 - (-4)) + 3(-6-4) = -3 + 16 - 30 = -17 \neq 0$. Calculate the adjoint matrix. $\text{adj}(A) = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -5 & -1 \\ -8 & -6 & 9 \\ -10 & 1 & 7 \end{pmatrix}$. $X = A^{-1}B = \frac{1}{-17} \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -5 & -1 \\ -8 & -6 & 9 \\ -10 & 1 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$. Solving gives $x=1, y=2, z=3$.

questions.question_text: Show that the volume of the greatest cylinder which can be inscribed in a cone of height $h$ and semi-vertical angle $\alpha$ is $\frac{4}{27} \pi h^3 \tan^2 \alpha$. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Let $x$ be the radius and $y$ the height of inscribed cylinder. By similar triangles in the cone section, $\frac{h-y}{x} = \cot \alpha \implies y = h - x \cot \alpha$. Volume $V = \pi x^2 y = \pi x^2(h - x \cot \alpha) = \pi(hx^2 - x^3 \cot \alpha)$. For maxima, $\frac{dV}{dx} = \pi(2hx - 3x^2 \cot \alpha) = 0 \implies x = \frac{2h}{3 \cot \alpha} = \frac{2h}{3} \tan \alpha$. $\frac{d^2V}{dx^2} < 0$. Max volume $V = \pi (\frac{2h}{3} \tan \alpha)^2 (h - \frac{2h}{3}) = \frac{4}{27} \pi h^3 \tan^2 \alpha$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the definite integral $\int_0^\pi \frac{x \tan x}{\sec x + \tan x} \, dx$. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Let $I = \int_0^\pi \frac{x \tan x}{\sec x + \tan x} \, dx$. Using property $x \to \pi - x$, $I = \int_0^\pi \frac{(\pi - x) \tan(\pi-x)}{\sec(\pi-x) + \tan(\pi-x)} \, dx$. Since $\tan(\pi-x) = -\tan x$ and $\sec(\pi-x) = -\sec x$, $I = \int_0^\pi \frac{(\pi - x) \tan x}{\sec x + \tan x} \, dx$. Adding both $I$'s gives $2I = \pi \int_0^\pi \frac{\tan x}{\sec x + \tan x} \, dx$. Multiply by $\sec x - \tan x$ to integrate $\tan x(\sec x - \tan x) = \sec x \tan x - \tan^2 x = \sec x \tan x - (\sec^2 x - 1)$. $2I = \pi [\sec x - \tan x + x]_0^\pi = \pi( ( -1 - 0 + \pi) - (1 - 0 + 0) ) = \pi(\pi - 2)$. Thus $I = \frac{\pi(\pi - 2)}{2}$.

questions.question_text: Using the method of integration, find the area of the region bounded by the triangle whose vertices are $(-1, 0), (1, 3)$ and $(3, 2)$. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Let $A(-1, 0), B(1, 3), C(3, 2)$. Equation of $AB$: $y - 0 = \frac{3-0}{1+1}(x+1) \implies y = \frac{3}{2}(x+1)$. Equation of $BC$: $y - 3 = \frac{2-3}{3-1}(x-1) \implies y = 3 - \frac{1}{2}(x-1)$. Equation of $AC$: $y - 0 = \frac{2-0}{3+1}(x+1) \implies y = \frac{1}{2}(x+1)$. Area = $\int_{-1}^1 \frac{3}{2}(x+1)\,dx + \int_1^3 (3 - \frac{1}{2}(x-1))\,dx - \int_{-1}^3 \frac{1}{2}(x+1)\,dx$. Evaluating integrals: $3 + 5 - 4 = 4$ sq units.

questions.question_text: Read the case context: A manufacturer produces three products $x, y, z$ which he sells in two markets. Annual sales are: Market I ($10000, 2000, 18000$) and Market II ($6000, 20000, 8000$). Unit sale prices are ₹2.50, ₹1.50, and ₹1.00 respectively. Determine the total revenue in each market using matrix algebra operations. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Represent quantities by matrix $Q = \begin{pmatrix} 10000 & 2000 & 18000 \\ 6000 & 20000 & 8000 \end{pmatrix}$ and prices by column matrix $P = \begin{pmatrix} 2.50 \\ 1.50 \\ 1.00 \end{pmatrix}$. Revenue $R = QP = \begin{pmatrix} 10000(2.5) + 2000(1.5) + 18000(1) \\ 6000(2.5) + 20000(1.5) + 8000(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 25000 + 3000 + 18000 \\ 15000 + 30000 + 8000 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 46000 \\ 53000 \end{pmatrix}$. Market I revenue is ₹46000, Market II is ₹53000.

questions.question_text: Read the case context: An architect is designing a square-based open-top rectangular water tank. The tank must hold exactly $4000 \text{ m}^3$ of water. The material for the base costs ₹50 per square meter, and the material for the four vertical sides costs ₹20 per square meter. Formulate the cost function and determine the optimal base dimensions to minimize cost using calculus. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Let base side be $x$ and height be $y$. Volume $x^2y = 4000 \implies y = 4000/x^2$. Total Cost $C = 50x^2 + 20(4xy) = 50x^2 + 80x(4000/x^2) = 50x^2 + 320000/x$. For minimum cost, $dC/dx = 100x - 320000/x^2 = 0 \implies x^3 = 3200 \implies x = 10\sqrt[3]{3.2} \approx 14.73$ m. Using second derivative test $d^2C/dx^2 = 100 + 640000/x^3 > 0$, confirming minimal cost construction.

questions.question_text: Read the case context: A mechanical engineering firm analyzes the velocity $v(t)$ of a new robotic arm over a 4-second period, modeled by $v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9$ (in m/s). Engineers need to know the total displacement from $t=0$ to $t=4$ seconds, as well as identify the specific time intervals where the robotic arm is moving backward (velocity is negative). [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Displacement is $\int_0^4 (3t^2 - 12t + 9) \, dt = [t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t]_0^4 = (64 - 96 + 36) - 0 = 4$ meters. To find when it moves backward, solve $v(t) < 0$. Factor to $3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 3(t-1)(t-3) < 0$. The robotic arm moves backward strictly during the interval $1 < t < 3$ seconds.
